source_cards.title: Beyond SDR: How Music Source Separation Reshapes Rhythm-Relevant Signal Properties
source_cards.bounded_summary: Across four separators on MUSDB18-HQ, onset placement was substantially more robust than drum transient and dynamic shape. SI-SDR did not reliably rank attack/envelope fidelity, and input context altered transient rendering.
limitations: No listening test linked measured attack distortion to perceived timing.
One checkpoint per architecture; MUSDB18-HQ and drums-centred analysis.
The transformer context result was marginal and fragile under leave-one-out analysis.

source_cards.title: MSS Drum Fidelity Evaluation
source_cards.bounded_summary: MIT-licensed pipeline exposes model/version/input provenance, cached separations, onset and dynamic-profile metrics, result tables, and scripts for reproducing the paper's benchmark and context-length sweep.
limitations: Code and audio experiments were inspected but not run.
MUSDB18-HQ audio is not stored in the repository.

source_cards.title: Where Is the Beat in That Note? Effects of Attack, Duration, and Frequency on the Perceived Timing of Musical and Quasi-Musical Sounds
source_cards.bounded_summary: Attack and duration were primary cues for P-centre location and variability; perceived rhythmic timing is a distribution shaped by envelope properties, not a single waveform-onset coordinate.
limitations: Publisher version was not read in full.
Laboratory musical/quasi-musical sounds do not directly prescribe rock-drum edit amounts.

source_cards.title: The Effect of Expert Performance Microtiming on Listeners' Experience of Groove in Swing or Funk Music
source_cards.bounded_summary: In two performed bass/drum excerpts, fully quantized and original microtiming both received high groove ratings, whereas exaggerated deviations reduced ratings; experts were more sensitive.
limitations: Only two 20-second funk/swing performances; not rock.
Self-report and bodily entrainment measures sometimes disagreed.
No universal milliseconds threshold follows from proportional manipulations.

source_cards.title: Automated Audio Time Alignment for Multi-Microphone Setups: An Open-Source Approach
source_cards.bounded_summary: Describes MATLAB and C++ VST tools for detecting/re-aligning multi-microphone delay and a MUSHRA evaluation of temporal realignment.
limitations: Full paper was not freely readable in this run.
No study result or numerical threshold is promoted from abstract-only access.

source_cards.title: Cubase Pro 15 Group Editing and Phase-Coherent AudioWarp documentation
source_cards.bounded_summary: Group Editing links matching events; Phase-Coherent AudioWarp must be explicitly enabled and requires matching event boundaries and common marker positions. Ordinary multi-track AudioWarp quantization does not maintain phase coherence.
limitations: DAW documentation, not a perceptual study.
Phase-coherent operation does not guarantee a musically preferable edit.

source_cards.title: Sound Radix Auto-Align 2 product documentation and release notes
source_cards.bounded_summary: Documents time alignment, spectral-phase optimization, polarity/group controls and four comparison slots; current release listed as 2.2.2.
limitations: Claims about punch, size and quality are vendor claims.
No independent listening result was obtained from these pages.

source_cards.title: AAM: a dataset of Artificial Audio Multitracks for diverse music information retrieval tasks
source_cards.bounded_summary: AAM contains 3,000 synthetic Western-pop-oriented mixes, per-instrument tracks, MIDI and precise annotations, useful for controlled algorithm tests but not representative of real human performances.
limitations: Synthetic composition and sampled instruments limit production realism.
Zenodo record license field was empty; audio reuse not approved here.

knowledge_cards.title: Onset fidelity is not transient fidelity
knowledge_cards.claim: A separator can preserve detected drum onset positions while changing attack slope, crest and dynamic variation; SDR or onset-F alone cannot validate rhythm-critical signal shape.

knowledge_cards.title: Perceived time depends on envelope
knowledge_cards.claim: Attack and duration contribute to a sound's perceptual centre and timing uncertainty, so sample-onset coincidence does not prove perceptual synchrony.

knowledge_cards.title: Quantization amount is stylistic and contextual
knowledge_cards.claim: Existing evidence does not support either mandatory microtiming or mandatory perfect quantization; exaggerated deviations are risky, but competent original and quantized timing can both groove.

knowledge_cards.title: Multi-mic edits must preserve channel relationships
knowledge_cards.claim: For a drum performance captured through multiple microphones, timing edits should move corresponding material together and keep one shared marker/edit structure unless a deliberate perspective change is being tested.

knowledge_cards.title: Phase-coherent AudioWarp is opt-in
knowledge_cards.claim: Cubase ordinary multi-track AudioWarp quantization is not phase-coherent; the dedicated Phase-Coherent mode has explicit event and marker preconditions.

knowledge_cards.title: Synthetic multitracks need domain and license gates
knowledge_cards.claim: Synthetic multitracks with exact annotations can test algorithms, but must not substitute for human rock performance validation; an empty repository license field blocks approval as a reusable audio reference.

candidate_rules.summary: Do not validate separated drum timing or dynamics from SDR/onset-F alone.
candidate_rules.when_to_apply: Any drum editing, groove, transient or dynamics analysis performed on a separated stem.
candidate_rules.what_to_change: Record separator name/version/input window; compare attack slope, crest and dynamic variation against legal ground truth or unseparated evidence before using the measurement.
candidate_rules.do_not_damage: Attack identity, dynamics, cymbal detail, perceived timing.
candidate_rules.how_to_verify: Repeat the same passage with fixed and varied context; compare onset-F and envelope descriptors; perform level-matched listening.
candidate_rules.cancel_if: Fall back to mixture/raw multitrack analysis when descriptor direction changes with model or input window.

candidate_rules.summary: Evaluate timing by perceptual centre as well as sample onset.
candidate_rules.when_to_apply: Aligning or transient-shaping kick, snare, bass or other rhythmic events.
candidate_rules.what_to_change: Keep onset, attack duration/slope and spectral-envelope context as separate measurements; audition corrections in the full rhythm section.
candidate_rules.do_not_damage: Natural attack, instrument identity, groove and punch.
candidate_rules.how_to_verify: Level-match; inspect waveform and envelope; blind-compare timing feel with full kit/bass.
candidate_rules.cancel_if: Undo if the edit makes attacks sound later/earlier, smaller or smeared despite closer onset coincidence.

candidate_rules.summary: Move all microphones of a performance together during timing edits.
candidate_rules.when_to_apply: Editing multi-mic drums or another source with shared bleed.
candidate_rules.what_to_change: Create one linked edit group and apply common slice/warp positions to all corresponding channels.
candidate_rules.do_not_damage: Inter-mic delay pattern, room perspective, overhead image, bleed continuity.
candidate_rules.how_to_verify: Check mono, polarity, correlation/lag stability and crossfades before and after; listen to the full kit.
candidate_rules.cancel_if: Undo if ambience moves, cymbals smear, mono thins or inter-channel lag becomes section-dependent.

candidate_rules.summary: In Cubase, use phase-coherent mode explicitly or prefer grouped slicing.
candidate_rules.what_to_change: Ensure equal event boundaries; enable Group Editing; use Slice as baseline or explicitly enable Phase-Coherent AudioWarp with common marker positions.
candidate_rules.do_not_damage: Phase coherence, transient onset, crossfade continuity.
candidate_rules.how_to_verify: Confirm mode state and event eligibility; render a short test; compare full kit and mono against the unedited source.
candidate_rules.cancel_if: Use grouped slicing or manual edits if Cubase warns, bounces unexpectedly, or the phase-coherent constraints are not satisfied.

candidate_rules.summary: Correct obvious timing errors without making the grid a universal target.
candidate_rules.when_to_apply: Pre-mix editing of drums/bass where deviations distract from the intended pulse.
candidate_rules.what_to_change: Preserve coherent performer patterns; test bounded reduction of outliers and section-level feel before full quantization.
candidate_rules.do_not_damage: Groove, push/pull, fills, phrase transitions and kick-bass relationship.
candidate_rules.how_to_verify: Compare original, partial correction and grid versions blind with expert listening; keep all versions level-matched.
candidate_rules.cancel_if: Undo or reduce the edit when groove, movement or section contrast weakens.

candidate_rules.summary: Treat automatic phase alignment as an auditable candidate, not a guaranteed improvement.
candidate_rules.when_to_apply: Stationary multi-microphone recordings with demonstrable shared content/bleed and comb filtering.
candidate_rules.what_to_change: Generate several alignment candidates including unchanged; store delay/polarity/spectral-phase choices and compare them.
candidate_rules.do_not_damage: Spatial intent, room depth, cymbal character, source directionality.
candidate_rules.how_to_verify: Use equal-loudness A/B, mono, full-band and band-limited checks; require repeatable preference across sections.
candidate_rules.cancel_if: Reject if benefit is section-specific, changes perspective, or depends only on louder low end.
